module-3-club-check-in-project.label: Module Project: Club Check-In Tracker
module-3-club-check-in-project.summary: Build one club check-in tracker cumulatively: process a known number of members, count accepted check-ins, count VIP names, switch to a sentinel-controlled loop, and finally skip blank entries safely.

mp_3.title: Keep the desk open until done

try-module-3-club-check-in-sketch0.title: Check in three members
try-module-3-club-check-in-sketch0.prompt: Read exactly three member names with a `for` loop and `range(3)`. After each input, print `Checked in: <name>`.
try-module-3-club-check-in-sketch0.hint: Put `input()` and the check-in print inside one `for _ in range(3):` loop.

help.concept: A fixed-count `for` loop is a good starting point when the desk knows exactly how many entries to process.
help.hint_1: Use `range(3)` so the loop runs exactly three times.
help.hint_2: Read and print one name during each iteration.

try-module-3-club-check-in-sketch0.starterCode: # Read exactly three member names and print one check-in line for each.

sourceChecks.message: Use one `for` loop with `range(3)` to read and print all three member names.

mp-1-check-in-three-members.title: Add the total check-in counter
mp-1-check-in-three-members.prompt: Keep the exact three-member check-in program. Add a counter named `total`, increase it once for each accepted input, and print `Total check-ins: <total>` after the loop.
mp-1-check-in-three-members.hint: Initialize `total = 0` before the loop and increment it once inside each iteration.

help.concept: A counter starts at zero and records how many times the repeated check-in action succeeds.
help.hint_1: Keep the existing `range(3)` loop and check-in line.
help.hint_2: Add `total += 1` inside the loop, then print the total after the loop.

mp-1-check-in-three-members.solutionCode:
total = 0
for _ in range(3):
    name = input()
    total += 1
    print(f"Checked in: {name}")

print(f"Total check-ins: {total}")

sourceChecks.message: Keep the fixed-count loop and add a total counter that increments once per member.

mp-2-count-vip-members.title: Count VIP members too
mp-2-count-vip-members.prompt: Keep the total counter working. Add `vip_count`, increase it only when a name starts with `VIP-`, and print both final counts after the loop.
mp-2-count-vip-members.hint: Initialize a second counter before the loop and update it under `if name.startswith("VIP-"):`.

help.concept: One loop can maintain independent counters for all accepted entries and for entries matching a condition.
help.hint_1: Do not remove the total counter from the previous step.
help.hint_2: Increment `vip_count` only for names whose prefix is exactly `VIP-`.

mp-2-count-vip-members.starterCode:
total = 0
for _ in range(3):
    name = input()
    total += 1
    print(f"Checked in: {name}")

print(f"Total check-ins: {total}")
mp-2-count-vip-members.solutionCode:
total = 0
vip_count = 0
for _ in range(3):
    name = input()
    total += 1
    if name.startswith("VIP-"):
        vip_count += 1
    print(f"Checked in: {name}")

print(f"Total check-ins: {total}")
print(f"VIP check-ins: {vip_count}")

sourceChecks.message: Preserve the total counter and add a conditional VIP counter using `startswith("VIP-")`.

mp-3-stop-on-done.title: Keep the desk open until done
mp-3-stop-on-done.prompt: Start from the exact fixed-count tracker. Change only the repetition rule: use `while True` so the desk accepts any number of names, and stop when the input is exactly `done`. Preserve both counters and the check-in output.
mp-3-stop-on-done.hint: Replace the `for` loop with `while True`, read one name, then check the `done` sentinel before counting it.

help.concept: A sentinel-controlled `while` loop is useful when the number of future entries is unknown.
help.hint_1: Put `if name == "done":` immediately after the input.
help.hint_2: Use `break` for the sentinel, then keep the total and VIP logic for normal names.

mp-3-stop-on-done.starterCode:
total = 0
vip_count = 0
for _ in range(3):
    name = input()
    total += 1
    if name.startswith("VIP-"):
        vip_count += 1
    print(f"Checked in: {name}")

print(f"Total check-ins: {total}")
print(f"VIP check-ins: {vip_count}")
mp-3-stop-on-done.solutionCode:
total = 0
vip_count = 0
while True:
    name = input()
    if name == "done":
        break
    total += 1
    if name.startswith("VIP-"):
        vip_count += 1
    print(f"Checked in: {name}")

print(f"Total check-ins: {total}")
print(f"VIP check-ins: {vip_count}")

sourceChecks.message: Use `while True` with a `done` sentinel and `break`, while preserving both counters.

mp-4-finish-club-check-in.title: Finish the club check-in tracker
mp-4-finish-club-check-in.prompt: Keep the sentinel tracker working. Add one final special case: if the input is empty, use `continue` so the blank entry is not printed or counted. `done` must still end the session. Print the total and VIP counts after the loop.
mp-4-finish-club-check-in.hint: Check `done` first, then check the empty string and `continue`, then do the normal counting work.

help.concept: Special cases belong before normal loop work when they should stop or skip the current iteration.
help.hint_1: The `done` sentinel should `break` before any counting happens.
help.hint_2: The empty string should `continue` before total or VIP counters change.

mp-4-finish-club-check-in.starterCode:
total = 0
vip_count = 0
while True:
    name = input()
    if name == "done":
        break
    total += 1
    if name.startswith("VIP-"):
        vip_count += 1
    print(f"Checked in: {name}")

print(f"Total check-ins: {total}")
print(f"VIP check-ins: {vip_count}")
mp-4-finish-club-check-in.solutionCode:
total = 0
vip_count = 0
while True:
    name = input()
    if name == "done":
        break
    if name == "":
        continue
    total += 1
    if name.startswith("VIP-"):
        vip_count += 1
    print(f"Checked in: {name}")

print(f"Total check-ins: {total}")
print(f"VIP check-ins: {vip_count}")

sourceChecks.message: Handle `done` with `break` and blank input with `continue` before counting normal names.
